claim: On neutral_hostile_v1/09_ml_artifacts, the promoted streamed G04 policy verifier owns nearly all canonical strong-verification wall time; the canonical manifest/member wrapper is not the dominant runtime owner.

decision.hypothesis: The canonical strong_verify wrapper's manifest validation and second per-user-member read is a dominant cause of the measured G04 extraction regression.
decision.reason: The canonical wrapper added only 4.016 ms median, 1.31% of canonical verification wall time. The promoted streamed policy verifier accounted for 98.69% of canonical verification time on the exact fixed ML G04 archive.
retire: Do not remove or weaken canonical manifest/member verification merely for speed; this experiment shows too little addressable wall-time headroom.
Do not move the timing boundary around the canonical wrapper to manufacture a runtime pass.
decision.next_question: Within the promoted streamed G04 verifier, which exact costs dominate: physical record decode/inverse transforms, repeated record/node reconstruction caused by bounded caches, hashing/integrity, or metadata/session opening? Attribute these components on the same fixed archive before changing product semantics.

scope: This is one-workload research attribution, not product or release evidence. It narrows the causal search for the G04 runtime regression and does not establish general transfer to every G04 archive or PrefixGraph/r24 path.
